# 3-Week Reconditioning Block: Return to Baseline

## Before You Start: Screening

The persistent fatigue is the main thing to watch. Strength returns quickly after 3 weeks off, but post-viral fatigue does not always respond well to load. Do these checks first.

**Pre-start screen (ask him directly):**
- Any chest pain, palpitations, unusual breathlessness, or dizziness since the flu? If yes, get GP clearance before training. Post-viral myocarditis is rare but is the one complication you cannot afford to miss.
- Has he seen a GP about the fatigue? If it has lasted more than 2 weeks past the acute illness, a quick check (bloods for iron/ferritin, thyroid, etc.) is reasonable alongside training.

**Daily readiness check (before each session):**
- **Morning resting HR:** If it is more than 7–10 bpm above his normal, do a recovery-only session (walk plus mobility).
- **Sleep and energy (1–5 scale):** If he scores 2 or below, drop the session by one "week" in intensity.
- **Post-exertional response:** If he feels markedly *worse* 24–48 hours after a session rather than just sore, hold or regress the progression. Repeated crashes mean stop and refer.

**Progression rule:** Only advance to the next week if the current week's top sets felt at or below the target RPE and he recovered normally. Otherwise repeat the week. A 4-week block that works beats a 3-week block that sets him back.

---

## Structure

The block uses three full-body sessions per week (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri) with at least one rest day between. Loads are based on his pre-illness numbers, but **RPE overrides percentages**. With 4kg lost, the bar may feel heavier than the numbers suggest.

- **Session A:** Squat focus plus Bench
- **Session B:** Deadlift focus plus Overhead Press
- **Session C:** Light Squat plus Bench volume

Each session starts with a 10-minute general warm-up (bike or rower, easy pace) followed by ramp-up sets.

---

## Week 1: Re-grooving (≈60–65%, RPE 5–6)

The goal this week is to restore movement patterns, tendon and connective tissue tolerance, and confidence. Every set should feel easy and crisp. He should finish feeling *better* than when he started.

**Session A**
- Back Squat: 3×6 @ 85–90kg
- Bench Press: 3×6 @ 60–65kg
- Chest-Supported Row: 3×10, moderate
- Split Squat: 2×8/leg, bodyweight or light dumbbells
- Plank: 2×30s

**Session B**
- Deadlift: 3×5 @ 100–110kg
- Overhead Press: 3×6, approx. 60% of his usual working weight
- Lat Pulldown: 3×10
- Back Extension: 2×10
- Face Pull: 2×15

**Session C**
- Back Squat: 2×5 @ 80kg (technique focus)
- Bench Press: 3×8 @ 57.5–60kg
- Dumbbell Row: 3×10/side
- Romanian Deadlift: 2×8, light
- Dead Bug: 2×8/side

**Conditioning:** 2–3 × 20–30 minutes of easy zone 2 work (conversational pace walking or cycling) on non-lifting days. No HIIT.

---

## Week 2: Rebuilding Capacity (≈70–77%, RPE 6–7)

This week adds volume and load. He should finish sets with 3 or more reps in reserve.

**Session A**
- Back Squat: 4×5 @ 100–107.5kg
- Bench Press: 4×5 @ 72.5–75kg
- Chest-Supported Row: 3×8–10
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 3×8/leg
- Hanging Knee Raise: 3×10

**Session B**
- Deadlift: 3×4 @ 120–130kg
- Overhead Press: 3×5, approx. 75% of his usual working weight
- Weighted or Assisted Pull-up: 3×6–8
- Back Extension: 3×10, loaded
- Face Pull: 3×15

**Session C**
- Back Squat: 3×5 @ 95kg
- Close-Grip or Paused Bench: 3×6 @ 65–70kg
- Dumbbell Row: 3×10/side
- Romanian Deadlift: 3×8, moderate
- Pallof Press: 3×10/side

**Conditioning:** 2–3 × 30 minutes of zone 2. If he is recovering well, one session can include 4–6 × 30-second moderate efforts.

---

## Week 3: Return to Working Weights (≈80–87%, RPE 7–8)

This week brings back heavier triples to re-sensitise him to load. There is no grinding and no true max testing.

**Session A**
- Back Squat: 4×3 @ 115–122.5kg
- Bench Press: 4×3 @ 82.5–87.5kg
- Barbell Row: 3×6–8
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 3×6/leg, heavier than Week 2
- Ab Wheel: 3×8

**Session B**
- Deadlift: 3×3 @ 140–147.5kg
- Overhead Press: 4×4, approx. 85% of his usual working weight
- Weighted Pull-up: 3×5–6
- Back Extension: 3×8, loaded
- Face Pull: 3×15

**Session C (end-of-block check, only if readiness is green)**
- Back Squat: Work up to a top single @ RPE 8 (expect around 125–130kg), then 2×3 @ 110kg
- Bench Press: Work up to a top single @ RPE 8 (expect around 90kg), then 2×5 @ 77.5kg
- Light RDL and core work only

Use the RPE-8 singles to judge where he stands. If he hits roughly 90% of his old numbers at RPE 8, he is effectively back to baseline strength and can resume normal programming. If not, run Week 3 again before moving on.

**Conditioning:** Maintain 2–3 zone 2 sessions. Full conditioning work can return next block.

---

## Nutrition: Regaining the 4kg

- **Calories:** Aim for a 300–500 kcal/day surplus above maintenance. A target of about 0.25–0.5kg per week is realistic. Much of the early regain will be glycogen and water, which is fine.
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, roughly 150–180g for most men his size, spread over 4 meals.
- **Carbohydrates:** Prioritise these around training. He needs the fuel, and under-eating will worsen the fatigue.
- **Hydration and micronutrients:** Focus on whole foods. If bloods show low iron or vitamin D, supplementing is worth considering, but leave that to the GP.
- **Tracking:** Weigh him 3× per week in the morning and use the weekly average.

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 hours. This is the single biggest lever for post-viral fatigue.
- **Stress outside the gym:** Keep life stress and alcohol low during the block.
- **Mobility:** 10 minutes of easy mobility or walking on off days rather than full rest, as long as his fatigue tolerates it.

## Red Flags: Stop and Refer

Stop training and refer him to a GP if any of the following occur:
- Chest pain, palpitations, or fainting
- Breathlessness out of proportion to effort
- Fatigue getting progressively worse across the block
- Repeated crashes after sessions (post-exertional malaise)
- Resting HR staying elevated for several days

Once he completes Week 3 with normal recovery, he should be ready to move into a standard intermediate block from roughly 90–95% of his previous training maxes.

# Week 1 Working Loads

These are based on 60–65% of his pre-illness maxes. Start at the **lower number** in Session A and move to the upper number only if RPE stays at 5–6.

## Back Squat (pre-illness 140kg)

| Session | Sets × Reps | Load | % of old max |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3×6 | **85kg**, up to 90kg | 61–64% |
| C | 2×5 | **80kg** | 57% |

**Ramp-up:** bar × 10, 50×5, 65×3, 75×2, then working sets.

## Bench Press (pre-illness 100kg)

| Session | Sets × Reps | Load | % of old max |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3×6 | **60kg**, up to 65kg | 60–65% |
| C | 3×8 | **57.5kg**, up to 60kg | 57–60% |

**Ramp-up:** bar × 10, 40×5, 50×3, then working sets.

## Deadlift (pre-illness 170kg)

| Session | Sets × Reps | Load | % of old max |
|---|---|---|---|
| B | 3×5 | **100kg**, up to 110kg | 59–65% |

**Ramp-up:** 60×5, 80×3, 90×2, then working sets.

---

## How to Apply Them

- **Session A sets the baseline.** If 85kg squat / 60kg bench feel like RPE 5 with clean bar speed, he can use the top of the range in later Week 1 sessions. If they feel like RPE 7 or higher, drop 5–10kg and keep the weight there for the week.
- **Bar speed is the best signal.** Every rep should move at roughly the same speed. If reps slow noticeably by the last set, the load is too heavy for this week.
- **Don't add sets or reps** even if he feels great. Week 1 is about tolerance, not stimulus. Judge how the week went by how he feels 24–48 hours after each session.
- **Overhead press:** use about 60% of his usual working weight. If he typically presses 60kg for sets of 5, that means 35–37.5kg.

# Adding Running: 3-Week Return to 10k

## Key Principles

**Aerobic fitness drops faster than strength.** After 3 weeks off plus illness, his running will feel harder than his lifting, so treat the two separately. He may be ready for 85% squats in Week 3 before he can comfortably run 10k.

**Running replaces the zone 2 work.** These runs take the place of the walks and bike sessions from the original plan. Don't stack both.

**Running counts toward his total fatigue.** Post-viral fatigue responds to total load, not just gym load. The daily readiness check covers runs too.

**Clarify his baseline.** "10k weekly" could mean one 10k run or 10km total across several runs. This plan builds to roughly 10km total by the end of the block. A continuous 10k run is the goal for the following 1–2 weeks.

---

## Weekly Layout

| Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lift A | Run | Lift B | Rest / walk | Lift C | Run | Rest |

In Weeks 2–3, a short third run can go on Thursday if he's recovering well.

- Keep runs off the day before deadlifts where possible. Tuesday is fine because it's easy volume.
- If a run and a lift must share a day, **lift first, run later** (ideally 6+ hours apart).

---

## Intensity Rule (All 3 Weeks)

**Every run is easy.** He should be able to speak in full sentences. If he has a heart rate monitor, stay in zone 2 (roughly 65–75% of max HR, or below his old easy-run HR).

- **Expect his pace to be slower** than before the illness at the same heart rate. That's normal. Slow down to hit the HR target rather than chasing old paces.
- **Cardiac drift is a warning sign.** If his HR keeps climbing at a steady easy pace (e.g. more than 10–15 bpm over 20 minutes on flat ground), end the run and walk home.
- **No intervals, tempo runs, or hills** until after the block.

---

## Week 1: Run-Walk (≈4–5km total)

**Tue:** 10 min brisk walk, then 6 × (3 min easy run / 1 min walk), then 5 min walk. About 2.5km of running.

**Sat:** Same session. If Tuesday felt easy and he recovered normally, progress to 5 × (4 min run / 1 min walk).

**Check:** He should feel fine the next morning and normal for Wednesday's deadlifts. If his legs or energy are noticeably worse, repeat this week's runs next week.

## Week 2: Continuous Easy Running (≈6–7km total)

**Tue:** 20–25 min continuous easy run (≈3–3.5km).

**Thu (optional, only on a green readiness day):** 15 min easy (≈2km). Skip it if Wednesday's deadlifts left him flat.

**Sat:** 25–30 min continuous easy run (≈4km).

## Week 3: Rebuilding Volume (≈8–10km total)

**Tue:** 25–30 min easy (≈4km).

**Thu (optional):** 15–20 min easy, plus 4 × 15-second relaxed strides at the end if he feels good.

**Sat:** 35–40 min easy (≈5–6km). This is his longest run of the block.

Keep in mind that Week 3 lifting is heavier. If Friday's top singles go ahead, keep Saturday's run strictly easy. Shorten it to 30 minutes if his legs are heavy.

## After the Block: The 10k

- **Week 4:** Runs of 4km, 3km, and 7–8km.
- **Week 5:** A continuous 10k at easy pace, provided the 8km run went well.

Build pace and intensity work back gradually after that.

---

## When to Cut Back

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Amber readiness (HR up, poor sleep, low energy) | Swap the run for a 20–30 min walk and keep the lift as planned (at reduced intensity per the earlier rules) |
| Red readiness | Rest day with walking only |
| Legs heavy before a lift | Cut the run's duration by a third |
| Worse 24–48 hours after a run (not just tired legs) | Repeat the previous week's running volume |

If he wants to push one goal harder, prioritise the lifting during these 3 weeks. Running volume is the easiest thing to trim without losing progress.

---

## Nutrition Adjustment

Running burns roughly 60–70 kcal per km at his size. By Week 3, that's an extra 500–700 kcal per week. **Add that on top of the 300–500 kcal daily surplus**, or the weight won't come back. The easiest approach is an extra carb-based snack on run days.

If his weekly average body weight stalls for 2 weeks, add another 200 kcal per day.

---

## Extra Red Flags for Running

Stop and refer to a GP if he has any of these, in addition to the earlier list:

- Breathlessness that seems out of proportion to an easy pace
- Chest tightness or palpitations while running
- Unusual HR spikes or irregular beats on his watch
- Dizziness during or after a run

# Nutrition Targets: Reconditioning Block

## Assumptions to Check

You didn't give his body weight or height, so these numbers assume **85kg pre-illness, 81kg now, about 180cm**. The method below lets you recalculate with his real figures.

Some of the 4kg is glycogen, water, and gut content, which come back within 1–2 weeks of normal eating. The rest is likely a mix of fat and some muscle. Expect the first 1.5–2kg to return quickly and the remainder more slowly.

---

## Step 1: Estimate Maintenance

**Mifflin-St Jeor (male):** 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5

At 81kg / 180cm / 41: 810 + 1,125 − 205 + 5 = **~1,735 kcal BMR**

Multiply by an activity factor of 1.55 for 3 lifts per week, runs, and a typical job: **~2,700 kcal maintenance.**

Treat this as a starting estimate. Adjust it using his weekly weight trend.

## Step 2: Add the Surplus

| Week | Training load | Daily target | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Light lifting, run-walk | **~3,000 kcal** | Maintenance + ~300 |
| 2 | Moderate lifting, ~6–7km running | **~3,100 kcal** | Surplus + run cost |
| 3 | Heavy lifting, ~8–10km running | **~3,200 kcal** | Surplus + run cost |

The aim is **0.25–0.5kg per week** after the initial quick rebound. Gaining faster than that mostly adds fat.

---

## Step 3: Macros (Week 2 Example, ~3,100 kcal)

| Macro | Target | Per kg | Calories |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Protein** | 160–170g | ~2.0 g/kg | ~660 |
| **Fat** | 75–85g | ~1.0 g/kg | ~720 |
| **Carbs** | 420–440g | ~5.3 g/kg | ~1,720 |

- **Protein** is fixed across all three weeks. Use 1.8–2.2 g/kg, which is 150–180g at his weight. It matters most for regaining lost muscle.
- **Fat** should stay at least 0.8 g/kg (about 65g) for hormonal health. Fat is also the easiest way to add calories if his appetite is poor.
- **Carbs** fill the rest of his calories. This is the macro that drives recovery from fatigue and restores glycogen, so don't cut it.

## Training vs Rest Days

Keep calories similar every day so the weight comes back steadily, but shift his carbs:

- **Lift or run days:** about 450–480g carbs, with a bit less fat
- **Rest days:** about 350–380g carbs, with a bit more fat

---

## Sample Day (~3,100 kcal, Lift Day)

| Meal | Example | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| Breakfast | 100g oats with milk, banana, honey, 3 eggs | ~40g |
| Mid-morning | Greek yoghurt (250g), granola, berries | ~25g |
| Lunch | 150g chicken, 250g cooked rice, veg, olive oil | ~50g |
| Pre-training (60–90 min before) | 2 slices toast with jam, or a bagel | ~10g |
| Post-training | Whey shake in milk, plus fruit | ~35g |
| Dinner | 180g salmon or lean beef, potatoes, veg | ~40g |
| Evening (optional) | Cottage cheese or casein, peanut butter on toast | ~25g |

---

## If His Appetite Is Still Low

This is common after a viral illness.

- **Use liquid calories.** Smoothies made with milk, oats, banana, peanut butter, and whey can provide 700–900 kcal without making him feel overly full.
- **Choose calorie-dense foods.** Nut butters, olive oil, cheese, dried fruit, whole milk, and granola all help.
- **Eat more often.** Five or six smaller meals are usually easier than three big ones.
- **Don't let fibre crowd out calories.** Include some white rice, pasta, and bread if large salads and veg are filling him up too much.

---

## Hydration and Supplements

- **Fluids:** About 35ml/kg/day as a baseline, which is roughly 2.8L, plus 500–750ml per hour of running. Pale urine is the target.
- **Creatine monohydrate (3–5g/day):** Worth considering. It's well evidenced, supports strength regain, and helps restore intramuscular water. Warn him it will add about 1kg on the scale early on.
- **Vitamin D:** Reasonable during the darker months. Ideally base it on his blood results.
- **Iron:** Only supplement if his bloods show it's low. Don't add it blindly.
- **Alcohol:** Keep it minimal. It impairs sleep and recovery, both of which are already limiting factors for him.

---

## Monitoring and Adjustment

Weigh him 3× per week, first thing in the morning, and use the **weekly average**.

| Weekly change (after Week 1) | Action |
|---|---|
| Less than 0.2kg gain | Add 200 kcal/day (mostly carbs) |
| 0.25–0.5kg gain | On track, hold steady |
| More than 0.7kg gain (excluding the Week 1 rebound and creatine) | Reduce by 150–200 kcal/day |
| Weight dropping | Check his actual intake first, then add 300 kcal/day |

**Week 1 note:** A jump of 1–2kg is expected. Don't cut calories in response to it.

**Fatigue link:** If his energy or session quality is poor while his weight is stalled, under-eating is the most likely cause. Raise his intake before reducing training.

By the end of the block he should have regained roughly 2.5–3.5kg. The final kilo usually comes back over the following 2–4 weeks at the same intake.

# Should He Skip Week 1?

**Short answer: no, not straight to pre-illness loads.** But his good day is useful information, and there's a sensible middle ground that respects it.

## Why "Feels Fine Today" Isn't Enough

**1. One good day isn't a trend.** Post-viral fatigue often fluctuates. The issue you flagged at intake was *persistent* fatigue, so a single normal day doesn't show it has resolved. The real test is how he responds 24–48 hours after training, and he hasn't been tested yet.

**2. Post-exertional crashes are delayed.** Feeling good before a session tells you nothing about how he'll feel two days after a heavy one. If he overreaches early, a crash can cost him 1–2 weeks, far more than Week 1 "costs" him.

**3. His body has changed.** He's 4kg lighter, has been mostly inactive for 3 weeks, and has been eating less. Pre-illness working weights are relative to a heavier, fitter version of him. Expect those loads to feel like RPE 8–9 rather than his usual 7, with more grinding and worse technique.

**4. Connective tissue lags behind muscle.** Tendons and ligaments detrain and re-adapt more slowly than muscle, and that difference matters more at 41. Most injuries in returning lifters happen when strength feels "back" but tissue tolerance isn't. Week 1 is largely for this.

**5. Myocarditis is unlikely but still worth respecting.** If you haven't yet asked about chest pain, palpitations, or unusual breathlessness, do that before any heavy session. Heavy straining is where an undetected cardiac issue would matter most.

## What He Actually Gains by Skipping

Very little. Strength after 3 weeks off comes back fast. The plan already has him near 85% with RPE-8 singles by Week 3. Skipping Week 1 might save him about a week. The downside risk is a setback of several weeks. That's a poor trade.

## A Reasonable Compromise

Use his good energy to **accelerate within the block** rather than skip it:

- **Start Week 1 at the top of the ranges:** squat 90kg, bench 65kg, deadlift 110kg. This is about 65%.
- **Run a quick load test in Session A:** after his working sets, do one extra set of 3 at around 75% (squat about 105kg, bench about 75kg). If bar speed is fast and it feels RPE 6 or below, that's evidence in his favour.
- **Compress Week 1 to one or two sessions.** If Session A goes well *and* he feels normal 48 hours later (resting HR normal, no crash), move straight into Week 2 loads from Session B or C.
- **Keep the running as planned.** His aerobic system detrains faster and is the more common source of post-viral setbacks. Don't accelerate both at once.

This approach could get him to Week 3 loads by around day 14 instead of day 21. That's most of what he wants, with the safety checks still in place.

## How to Frame It for Him

Something like:

> "Feeling good today is great, and we'll use it. We'll start at the top of the range and test you. If you handle it and feel normal two days later, we jump ahead. What we won't do is load you at 100% before we know how your body recovers, because a crash now costs more time than this whole week."

Intermediate lifters usually accept this well when they understand that the plan *responds* to how they're doing rather than holding them back.

## Bottom Line

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Straight to pre-illness loads | Not reasonable. High risk, small gain |
| Full Week 1 as written | Safe, but possibly overly conservative given how he feels |
| **Top-of-range Week 1 with a load test, advancing early if recovery is normal** | **Recommended** |

# Readiness for Full Intensity: The Signals

"Full intensity" means work at RPE 9+: heavy singles near max, AMRAPs, grinding sets, intervals, tempo runs, hills. Clear him for it when **several independent signals line up over at least a week**, not when one session goes well. That's the same principle you used to decide against skipping Week 1.

He needs to be green in four areas: **performance, recovery, physiology, and subjective state.**

---

## 1. Performance Signals (Gym)

| Signal | Green light | Not yet |
|---|---|---|
| **RPE-8 singles (Week 3, Session C)** | Squat ≥125kg, bench ≥90kg, deadlift ≥152kg (about 90% of old max) | Below about 85% |
| **Load vs RPE matching** | Week 3 triples feel at or below target RPE (7–8) | Prescribed loads consistently feel 1–2 RPE harder than planned |
| **Bar speed** | Consistent across sets, with no big drop-off on the last set | Reps slow noticeably by set 3–4 |
| **Technique under load** | Same positions as pre-illness: depth, bar path, bracing | Form breaks at 80–85% |
| **Session-to-session trend** | Each session is equal to or better than the last | Performance flat or declining despite holding the same loads |

**Strongest single indicator:** when his RPE-8 single predicts a max (using the rough rule that RPE 8 ≈ 92–94% of max) within about 5% of his old numbers, his strength is effectively back.

## 2. Performance Signals (Running)

| Signal | Green light | Not yet |
|---|---|---|
| **HR at easy pace** | Back to or near his pre-illness easy-run HR at a given pace | Still 8–10+ bpm higher than before |
| **Cardiac drift** | HR stays stable (within about 5–8 bpm) over a 40-minute easy run | HR climbs steadily at constant pace |
| **Longest run** | 7–8km continuous at easy effort, feeling comfortable | Struggling to finish, or needing walk breaks |
| **HR recovery** | Drops 20+ bpm in the first minute after stopping | Slow drop, or stays elevated |

Running intensity (intervals, tempo) may clear **later** than lifting intensity. That's expected. Clear each one separately.

## 3. Recovery Signals (The Most Important Category)

This is where post-viral setbacks show up, so weight it most heavily.

- **24–48 hour response:** after his hardest sessions (Week 3 heavy triples, longest run), he feels normally tired or sore but **not worse in energy, mood, or sleep**. This needs to hold across **at least 4–6 consecutive sessions**, not just one.
- **No delayed crashes:** zero episodes of "felt fine in the session, wiped out two days later" during Weeks 2–3.
- **Soreness resolves normally:** within 48–72 hours, as it did pre-illness.
- **Back-to-back tolerance:** he handles a lift and a run within 24 hours without the second one suffering badly.

**Any single post-exertional crash in the last 7–10 days resets the clock.** Hold intensity at the current level for another week.

## 4. Physiological Signals (Track Daily)

| Marker | Green light |
|---|---|
| **Morning resting HR** | Back to his pre-illness baseline (within 2–3 bpm) for 7+ consecutive days |
| **HRV (if he has a wearable)** | Back within his normal range, stable rather than swinging day to day |
| **Body weight** | Stable or rising. At least half the lost 4kg regained is a good sign |
| **Sleep** | 7+ hours, waking refreshed most days |

Resting HR is the simplest objective marker you have. If it's still elevated, he isn't fully recovered, however good he feels.

## 5. Subjective Signals

- Energy is **consistently** normal, meaning 5+ days per week rated 4–5 out of 5, not one good day.
- Motivation to train is normal, and he's looking forward to sessions rather than dragging himself in.
- No lingering cough, congestion, or "heavy" feeling in the chest.
- Appetite has returned to normal.

---

## The Clearance Checklist

Clear him for full intensity when **all** of these are true:

- [ ] RPE-8 singles at ≥90% of pre-illness maxes
- [ ] Prescribed Week 3 loads felt at or below target RPE
- [ ] No post-exertional crash in the last 7–10 days
- [ ] Resting HR at baseline for 7+ days
- [ ] Energy consistently normal (not just one day)
- [ ] Weight stable or rising
- [ ] No cardiac or respiratory symptoms at any point (chest pain, palpitations, disproportionate breathlessness)

For running intensity, also check:

- [ ] Easy-run HR close to pre-illness levels
- [ ] Minimal cardiac drift on a 40-minute run
- [ ] 7–8km continuous run completed comfortably

**If one or two boxes are unticked:** repeat Week 3 and recheck. **If the fatigue boxes keep failing after 4–6 weeks total:** refer to his GP, as discussed earlier.

---

## Reintroduce Intensity in Stages, Not All at Once

Even once he's cleared, don't jump straight to max testing and hard intervals in the same week.

**Week 4 (first post-block week):**
- Return to his normal intermediate programme at **90–95% of old training maxes**
- Allow RPE 8–9 top sets, but no true maxes yet
- Runs: add 4–6 strides; keep everything else easy (as planned for the 10k build)

**Week 5:**
- Normal programming at full training maxes
- One quality run: a short tempo run (e.g. 15–20 min at comfortably hard) **or** light intervals, not both
- Continue the readiness checks

**Week 6 onward:**
- Max testing is fine if his programme calls for it
- Full conditioning work
- Daily readiness checks can drop to resting HR only, unless something changes

**Keep the "worse 24–48 hours later" rule running through Weeks 4–6.** Intensity is a new stressor, and post-viral setbacks can still surface when it's first reintroduced.

---

## Bottom Line

He's ready when **performance is back, recovery is normal, and resting HR agrees, consistently for a week or more**. Feeling good is necessary but not sufficient. The recovery response to hard work is what really tells you. Realistically, with the plan as written, most people in his situation clear for lifting intensity around **weeks 4–5** and running intensity around **weeks 5–6**.

# Adding a 1RM Test to Week 3

**My recommendation: don't run a true 1RM in Week 3.** You can still reset his programme off solid numbers. Below is why, a better alternative, and a gated protocol if you decide to test anyway. You know the client, so it's your call.

## The Case Against Testing in Week 3

**1. It conflicts with the clearance criteria.** We set true maxes for Week 6 or later, after he's shown 4–6 sessions of normal recovery. In the back half of Week 3 he'll have only one week of RPE 7–8 work behind him. A max attempt is the biggest single stressor in the block, and the most likely trigger for a delayed crash.

**2. The number will be artificially low.** He's 4kg light, his glycogen is still refilling, and his nervous system hasn't been near max loads for 6 weeks. A Week 3 max will likely underestimate his true capacity by 5–10%. That number would be stale within 2–3 weeks.

**3. Under-loading is the realistic outcome.** Programming off a depressed max means Weeks 4–8 are too light. That defeats the point of using "real numbers."

**4. There's a cardiovascular consideration.** Maximal efforts involve heavy bracing and large blood pressure spikes. That's the scenario where an undetected post-viral cardiac issue matters most. Only test if he has been screened clean for chest pain, palpitations, and disproportionate breathlessness.

---

## Recommended Alternative: Estimated 1RM from the RPE-8 Singles

Session C already has him working up to RPE-8 singles. Add deadlift to that approach and you get reliable estimates without the max-effort cost.

**Formula:** e1RM ≈ RPE-8 single ÷ 0.92

| Lift | Example RPE-8 single | Estimated 1RM | Training max (90%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Squat | 127.5kg | ~138kg | ~125kg |
| Bench | 90kg | ~98kg | ~87.5kg |
| Deadlift | 155kg | ~168kg | ~150kg |

- This is accurate to within about 3–5% for an intermediate lifter who rates RPE honestly.
- Run his first post-block cycle off these training maxes.
- Retest with a true 1RM at around Week 6–8, once the remaining weight and conditioning are back. That number will reflect his real capacity.

**To add deadlift:** in Week 3 Session B, replace the 3×3 with a work-up to an RPE-8 single, followed by 2×3 at about 140kg.

---

## If You Still Want a True 1RM: Gated Protocol

### Prerequisites (all must be true on test day)

- [ ] Cardiac and respiratory screening completed and clear
- [ ] Week 3 Session A triples felt at or below RPE 8, with consistent bar speed
- [ ] No post-exertional crash at any point in Weeks 2–3
- [ ] Resting HR at baseline on the morning of the test
- [ ] Readiness score of 4–5 out of 5, with good sleep the night before
- [ ] Weight stable or rising

**If any box is unticked, revert to the e1RM method.** Don't test "to see how it goes."

### Restructured Week 3

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Session A, with triples reduced to 3×3 (squat 115kg, bench 82.5kg) |
| Tue | Easy run, 25–30 min |
| Wed | Rest, or 20 min walk |
| **Thu** | **Deadlift 1RM test**, then light OHP 3×5 at about 70% and face pulls |
| Fri | Rest |
| **Sat** | **Squat and bench 1RM test** |
| Sun | Rest, or an easy 20 min walk |

**Running changes:** drop the optional Thursday run and move Saturday's long run into Week 4. He shouldn't run hard or long within 24 hours of a test.

### Testing Protocol

**General rules for all lifts:**
- Use 3–5 minutes rest between heavy singles.
- Allow a maximum of 3 attempts after warm-up.
- **No missed reps.** Stop at the last clean lift. If an attempt feels like RPE 9.5, that's his max for the day.
- Stop immediately if technique breaks: depth lost, hips shooting up, or bar path drifting.
- Use safeties for squat and bench, plus a competent spotter.

**Deadlift (Thursday)**
- Warm-up: 60×5, 100×3, 120×2, 135×1, 145×1
- Opener: 152.5–155kg
- Second attempt: 160–165kg if the opener moved well
- Third attempt: 167.5–170kg, only if the second felt RPE 9 or below

**Squat (Saturday)**
- Warm-up: bar×10, 60×5, 85×3, 105×2, 117.5×1
- Opener: 125–127.5kg
- Second attempt: 132.5–135kg
- Third attempt: 137.5–140kg, only if the second felt RPE 9 or below

**Bench (Saturday, after squat with a 15 min break)**
- Warm-up: bar×10, 50×5, 65×3, 77.5×2, 85×1
- Opener: 90kg
- Second attempt: 95kg
- Third attempt: 97.5–100kg, only if the second felt RPE 9 or below

Don't chase his pre-illness numbers. If he hits around 90–95% of them, that's a good result at this point in his recovery.

### After the Test

- **Monitor for 72 hours.** Track resting HR, energy, and sleep, the same as after every session.
- **If he crashes,** treat Week 4 as a repeat of Week 2 loading and discount the test numbers by 5%. They were likely affected by fatigue.
- **Set training maxes at 90% of the tested 1RM.**
- **Plan an upward correction.** Because a Week 3 test likely underestimates his capacity, add 2.5kg to squat and deadlift and 1–2.5kg to bench training maxes after the first 2–3 weeks if sessions feel easy. Alternatively, retest at Week 8.

---

## Bottom Line

| Option | Accuracy for programming | Risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| e1RM from RPE-8 singles (Week 3), true max at Week 6–8 | High, and more representative | Low | **Recommended** |
| True 1RM in Week 3 with the gates above | Likely 5–10% low | Moderate | Acceptable if every gate is passed |
| True 1RM in Week 3 without gates | Low | High | Not advised |

If his goal is "real numbers," the e1RM gives you those now, and a Week 6–8 test gives you numbers that reflect where he actually is once he's recovered.

# 3-Week Reconditioning Block: Consolidated Programme

**Client:** 41M, intermediate lifter, returning after 3 weeks off with flu. He has persistent fatigue and 4kg of weight loss.
**Pre-illness maxes:** Bench 100kg, Squat 140kg, Deadlift 170kg. Ran about 10km per week.
**Goal:** Return to baseline strength and rebuild running, with an estimated 1RM reset at the end of Week 3.

---

## Part 1: Before Day 1

### Screening (complete before any loaded session)

- **Cardiac and respiratory check.** Ask about chest pain, palpitations, unusual breathlessness, dizziness or fainting since the flu. If he reports any of these, get GP clearance before training. Post-viral myocarditis is rare but must not be missed. This screen matters most for heavy straining work.
- **GP review of fatigue.** If the fatigue has lasted more than 2 weeks past the acute illness, recommend bloods (iron/ferritin, thyroid, vitamin D) alongside training.
- **Baseline data.** Record his actual body weight and height so you can recalculate the nutrition numbers. Also record his normal resting HR and his pre-illness easy-run HR and pace if he knows them. Confirm whether "10k weekly" meant one 10k run or 10km total.

### Daily Readiness Check (before every lift and every run)

| Marker | Green | Amber | Red |
|---|---|---|---|
| Morning resting HR | Within 5 bpm of normal | 5–10 bpm above | More than 10 bpm above |
| Energy/sleep (1–5) | 4–5 | 3 | 2 or below |
| 24–48h after last session | Normal tiredness/soreness | Heavier than expected | Markedly worse energy, mood or sleep |

- **Green:** Train as written.
- **Amber:** Lift at the previous week's loads. Swap the run for a 20–30 min walk.
- **Red:** Recovery day only (walk plus mobility).

### Progression Rule

Advance to the next week only if the current week's top sets felt at or below target RPE and recovery was normal. Otherwise repeat the week. **RPE overrides percentages throughout.** At 4kg lighter, the bar will feel heavier than the numbers suggest.

---

## Part 2: Weekly Structure

| Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lift A | Easy run | Lift B | Rest / walk (optional run in Wks 2–3) | Lift C | Easy run | Rest |

- **Session A:** Squat focus plus bench
- **Session B:** Deadlift focus plus overhead press
- **Session C:** Light squat plus bench volume (Week 3: RPE-8 singles)
- **Warm-up for every lift:** 10 min easy bike or rower, then the ramp-up sets listed.
- **Running replaces all zone 2 work** from the original plan. Don't stack walks or bike sessions on top of the runs.
- If a run and a lift fall on the same day, lift first and run later, ideally 6+ hours apart.

---

## Part 3: Week 1 – Re-grooving (≈65%, RPE 5–6), Accelerated Entry

**Adjustment:** He feels good, so Week 1 starts at the top of the ranges and includes a load test. He can move into Week 2 early if he earns it. **Pre-illness loads are not used.**

### Session A (Mon)
- **Back Squat:** 3×6 @ **90kg**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 50×5, 65×3, 75×2
  - **Load test:** after working sets, 1×3 @ **105kg**
- **Bench Press:** 3×6 @ **65kg**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 40×5, 50×3
  - **Load test:** after working sets, 1×3 @ **75kg**
- Chest-Supported Row: 3×10, moderate
- Split Squat: 2×8/leg, bodyweight or light dumbbells
- Plank: 2×30s

**Load test pass:** Bar speed is fast and consistent, and the set feels RPE 6 or below.
**Load test fail:** The set feels RPE 7 or above or slows down. In that case, drop working loads to 85kg squat and 60kg bench for the rest of the week.

### Session B (Wed)
- **Deadlift:** 3×5 @ **110kg**
  - Ramp: 60×5, 80×3, 90×2, 100×1
- **Overhead Press:** 3×6 @ about 60% of his usual working weight (e.g. 35–37.5kg if he normally presses 60kg×5)
- Lat Pulldown: 3×10
- Back Extension: 2×10
- Face Pull: 2×15

### Session C (Fri)
- **Back Squat:** 2×5 @ **80kg** (technique focus)
- **Bench Press:** 3×8 @ **57.5–60kg**
- Dumbbell Row: 3×10/side
- Romanian Deadlift: 2×8, light
- Dead Bug: 2×8/side

### Early-Advance Rule

If **all** of the following are true, switch to Week 2 loads from Session B or C:
- Session A load test passed
- Resting HR is normal 48h after Session A
- No post-exertional crash
- Readiness is green

This can bring Week 3 loading forward to around day 14. Don't skip or shorten Week 2 or Week 3 themselves, and **don't accelerate the running**.

### Week 1 Running: Run-Walk (≈4–5km total)
- **Tue:** 10 min brisk walk, then 6 × (3 min easy run / 1 min walk), then 5 min walk (≈2.5km running)
- **Sat:** Repeat Tuesday's session. If Tuesday felt easy and recovery was normal, progress to 5 × (4 min run / 1 min walk).
- **Check:** He should feel normal the next morning and for the next lift. If not, repeat these runs in Week 2.

Leave 3+ reps in reserve on every set.

- Back Extension: 3×10, loaded
- Face Pull: 3×15

### Session C

- **Close-Grip or Paused Bench:** 3×6 @ **65–70kg**
- Dumbbell Row: 3×10/side
- Romanian Deadlift: 3×8, moderate
- Pallof Press: 3×10/side

### Week 2 Running: Continuous Easy (≈6–7km total)

- **Sat:** 25–30 min continuous easy run (≈4km)

---

## Part 5: Week 3 – Return to Working Weights plus e1RM Reset (≈80–87%, RPE 7–8)

**Adjustment:** No true 1RM in this block. Instead, he works up to RPE-8 singles on all three lifts to generate estimated maxes (e1RM). The deadlift single replaces the original 3×3 in Session B.

### Session A
- **Back Squat:** 4×3 @ **115–122.5kg**
- **Bench Press:** 4×3 @ **82.5–87.5kg**
- Barbell Row: 3×6–8
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 3×6/leg, heavier than Week 2
- Ab Wheel: 3×8

### Session B: Deadlift e1RM
- **Deadlift:**
  - Ramp: 60×5, 100×3, 120×2, 135×1
  - Work up in 5–10kg jumps to a **top single @ RPE 8** (expect about 150–155kg)
  - Then 2×3 @ **140kg**
- **Overhead Press:** 4×4 @ about 85% of his usual working weight
- Weighted Pull-up: 3×5–6
- Back Extension: 3×8, loaded
- Face Pull: 3×15

### Session C: Squat and Bench e1RM (green readiness only)
- **Back Squat:**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 60×5, 85×3, 105×2, 117.5×1
  - Work up to a **top single @ RPE 8** (expect about 125–130kg)
  - Then 2×3 @ **110kg**
- **Bench Press:**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 50×5, 65×3, 77.5×2
  - Work up to a **top single @ RPE 8** (expect about 90kg)
  - Then 2×5 @ **77.5kg**
- Light RDL: 2×8
- Core: 2 sets of choice

**Rules for the singles:**
- Use safeties and a spotter.
- RPE 8 means he could have done about 2 more reps. Stop there and don't chase numbers.
- If readiness is amber or red, postpone the singles to the next green day or run Week 3 again.

### Calculating His Numbers

**e1RM ≈ RPE-8 single ÷ 0.92. Training max (TM) = 90% of e1RM.**

| Lift | Example RPE-8 single | e1RM | Training max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Squat | 127.5kg | ~138kg | ~125kg |
| Bench | 90kg | ~98kg | ~87.5kg |
| Deadlift | 155kg | ~168kg | ~150kg |

Replace these examples with his actual singles.

### Week 3 Running: Rebuilding Volume (≈8–10km total)
- **Tue:** 25–30 min easy (≈4km)
- **Thu (optional):** 15–20 min easy, plus 4 × 15s relaxed strides if he feels good
- **Sat:** 35–40 min easy (≈5–6km), the longest run of the block
  - This follows Friday's singles, so keep it strictly easy.
  - Cut it to 30 min if his legs are heavy.

---

## Part 6: Running Rules (All Weeks)

- **Every run is easy.** He should be able to talk in full sentences, ideally in zone 2 (65–75% of max HR or below his old easy-run HR).
- **Slower pace is expected.** Run to heart rate, not to his old paces.
- **Cardiac drift.** If HR climbs more than 10–15 bpm over 20 min at a steady easy pace on flat ground, stop and walk home.
- **No intervals, tempo runs or hills** during the block.

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Amber readiness | Swap the run for a 20–30 min walk |
| Red readiness | Walk only |
| Legs heavy before a lift | Cut the run's duration by a third |
| Worse 24–48h after a run | Repeat the previous week's running volume |

**Priority:** If something has to give, keep the lifting and trim the running. Running volume is the easiest thing to cut without losing progress.

---

## Part 7: Nutrition

**Assumptions:** 85kg pre-illness, 81kg now, 180cm. Recalculate with his real figures.
**Maintenance estimate:** Mifflin-St Jeor BMR of about 1,735 kcal × 1.55 activity factor ≈ **2,700 kcal**.

### Daily Targets

| Week | Calories | Protein | Fat | Carbs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~3,000 | 160–170g | 75–85g | ~390g |
| 2 | ~3,100 | 160–170g | 75–85g | 420–440g |
| 3 | ~3,200 | 160–170g | 75–85g | ~450–470g |

These totals already include the extra calories for running (about 60–70 kcal per km).

- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg, spread across 4–5 meals of 30–50g each.
- **Fat:** At least 0.8 g/kg (about 65g minimum).
- **Carbs:** Fill the remaining calories. This is the macro that fixes fatigue and refills glycogen, so don't cut it.
- **Carb shifting:**
  - Lift or run days: about 450–480g carbs, slightly less fat
  - Rest days: about 350–380g carbs, slightly more fat
  - Keep total calories roughly equal every day.

### Sample Day (~3,100 kcal, lift day)

| Meal | Example | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| Breakfast | 100g oats with milk, banana, honey, 3 eggs | ~40g |
| Mid-morning | 250g Greek yoghurt, granola, berries | ~25g |
| Lunch | 150g chicken, 250g cooked rice, veg, olive oil | ~50g |
| Pre-training (60–90 min before) | Bagel or 2 slices toast with jam | ~10g |
| Post-training | Whey shake in milk, plus fruit | ~35g |
| Dinner | 180g salmon or lean beef, potatoes, veg | ~40g |
| Evening (optional) | Cottage cheese or casein, peanut butter on toast | ~25g |

### If His Appetite Is Low
- Use smoothies made with milk, oats, banana, peanut butter and whey (700–900 kcal each).
- Lean on calorie-dense foods: nut butter, olive oil, cheese, dried fruit, whole milk.
- Eat 5–6 smaller meals instead of 3 large ones.
- Include white rice, pasta and bread so fibre doesn't fill him up before he hits his calories.

### Fluids and Supplements
- **Fluids:** About 2.8L/day baseline, plus 500–750ml per hour of running.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3–5g/day. Warn him it adds about 1kg on the scale early on.
- **Vitamin D:** Ideally based on bloods; reasonable in darker months.
- **Iron:** Only if his bloods show it's low.
- **Alcohol:** Keep it minimal.

### Monitoring

Weigh him 3× per week, first thing in the morning, and use the weekly average.

| Weekly change (after Week 1) | Action |
|---|---|
| Less than 0.2kg gain | Add 200 kcal/day, mostly carbs |
| 0.25–0.5kg gain | On track, hold steady |
| More than 0.7kg gain (excluding rebound and creatine) | Reduce by 150–200 kcal/day |
| Weight dropping | Check his actual intake first, then add 300 kcal/day |

- **Week 1:** A 1–2kg jump is expected. Don't cut calories in response.
- **Fatigue link:** If he feels poor and his weight has stalled, increase food before reducing training.
- **Expected outcome:** About 2.5–3.5kg regained by the end of the block. The rest usually returns over the following 2–4 weeks.

---

## Part 8: Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 hours. This is the biggest lever for post-viral fatigue.
- **Off days:** 10 min of mobility or an easy walk rather than complete rest, if his fatigue allows.
- **Life stress and alcohol:** Keep both low during the block.

---

## Part 9: Red Flags – Stop and Refer to GP

- Chest pain or tightness, palpitations, irregular beats on his watch, fainting or dizziness
- Breathlessness out of proportion to effort, including at easy running pace
- Resting HR elevated for several consecutive days
- Fatigue getting progressively worse across the block
- Repeated post-exertional crashes
- Fatigue boxes still failing after 4–6 weeks in total

---

## Part 10: End-of-Block Clearance

He is cleared for full-intensity lifting (RPE 9+, true maxes) when **all** of these are true:

- [ ] RPE-8 singles at 90% or more of pre-illness maxes (squat ≥125kg, bench ≥90kg, deadlift ≥152kg)
- [ ] Week 3 loads felt at or below target RPE, with consistent bar speed and normal technique
- [ ] No post-exertional crash in the last 7–10 days (any crash resets the clock)
- [ ] Resting HR at baseline for 7+ consecutive days; HRV stable if tracked
- [ ] Energy normal on 5+ days per week
- [ ] Weight stable or rising
- [ ] No cardiac or respiratory symptoms at any point

**For running intensity, also require:**
- [ ] Easy-run HR close to pre-illness levels
- [ ] HR drift of 8 bpm or less over a 40-min easy run
- [ ] 7–8km continuous run completed comfortably

If one or two boxes are unticked, repeat Week 3 and recheck.

---

## Part 11: After the Block (Weeks 4–8)

| Week | Lifting | Running |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Normal intermediate programme from the e1RM-based training maxes. RPE 8–9 top sets, no maxes. | 4km, 3km, 7–8km, all easy, plus 4–6 strides |
| 5 | Full training maxes | Continuous easy 10k (if the 8km went well). One quality session: short tempo **or** light intervals, not both. |
| 6+ | Max work allowed if all clearance boxes are ticked | Full conditioning returns |
| 6–8 | **True 1RM retest** to correct the training maxes upward | — |

- Keep the "worse 24–48 hours later" rule running through Weeks 4–6.
- If early sessions feel easy, add 2.5kg to squat and deadlift training maxes and 1–2.5kg to bench after 2–3 weeks.

---

## Appendix: Gated True 1RM in Week 3 (Optional, Not Recommended)

Use this only if you decide to override the e1RM approach. **Every gate must be met on test day:**
- Cardiac screen completed and clear
- Session A triples at RPE 8 or below
- No crashes in Weeks 2–3
- Resting HR at baseline that morning
- Readiness 4–5 with good sleep the night before
- Weight stable or rising

If any gate fails, revert to the e1RM method.

**Restructured Week 3**

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Session A, reduced to 3×3 (squat 115kg, bench 82.5kg) |
| Tue | Easy run, 25–30 min |
| Wed | Rest or 20 min walk |
| Thu | Deadlift 1RM test, then OHP 3×5 @ about 70% and face pulls |
| Fri | Rest |
| Sat | Squat 1RM test, then bench 1RM test (15 min break between) |
| Sun | Rest or easy walk |

Drop the Thursday run and move the long run into Week 4.

**Test rules:**
- 3–5 min rest between singles
- Maximum of 3 attempts after warm-up
- No missed reps; stop at RPE 9.5 or at any technique breakdown
- Safeties and a spotter required

| Lift | Warm-up | Opener | Second | Third (only if 2nd ≤ RPE 9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deadlift | 60×5, 100×3, 120×2, 135×1, 145×1 | 152.5–155kg | 160–165kg | 167.5–170kg |
| Squat | bar×10, 60×5, 85×3, 105×2, 117.5×1 | 125–127.5kg | 132.5–135kg | 137.5–140kg |
| Bench | bar×10, 50×5, 65×3, 77.5×2, 85×1 | 90kg | 95kg | 97.5–100kg |

**After the test:**
- Monitor resting HR, energy and sleep for 72 hours.
- If he crashes, run Week 4 as a repeat of Week 2 loading and discount the tested numbers by 5%.
- Set training maxes at 90% of the tested 1RMs.
- Expect these numbers to be 5–10% low, and correct them upward by Week 8.

# 3-Week Reconditioning Block: Consolidated Programme

**Client:** 41M, intermediate lifter, returning after 3 weeks off with flu. He has persistent fatigue and 4kg of weight loss.
**Pre-illness maxes:** Bench 100kg, Squat 140kg, Deadlift 170kg. Ran about 10km per week.
**Goal:** Return to baseline strength and rebuild running, with an estimated 1RM reset at the end of Week 3.

---

## Part 1: Before Day 1

### Screening (complete before any loaded session)

- **Cardiac and respiratory check.** Ask about chest pain, palpitations, unusual breathlessness, dizziness or fainting since the flu. If he reports any of these, get GP clearance before training. Post-viral myocarditis is rare but must not be missed. This screen matters most for heavy straining work.
- **GP review of fatigue.** If the fatigue has lasted more than 2 weeks past the acute illness, recommend bloods (iron/ferritin, thyroid, vitamin D) alongside training.
- **Baseline data.** Record his actual body weight and height so you can recalculate the nutrition numbers. Also record his normal resting HR and his pre-illness easy-run HR and pace if he knows them. Confirm whether "10k weekly" meant one 10k run or 10km total.

### Daily Readiness Check (before every lift and every run)

| Marker | Green | Amber | Red |
|---|---|---|---|
| Morning resting HR | Within 5 bpm of normal | 5–10 bpm above | More than 10 bpm above |
| Energy/sleep (1–5) | 4–5 | 3 | 2 or below |
| 24–48h after last session | Normal tiredness/soreness | Heavier than expected | Markedly worse energy, mood or sleep |

- **Green:** Train as written.
- **Amber:** Lift at the previous week's loads. Swap the run for a 20–30 min walk.
- **Red:** Recovery day only (walk plus mobility).

### Progression Rule

Advance to the next week only if the current week's top sets felt at or below target RPE and recovery was normal. Otherwise repeat the week. **RPE overrides percentages throughout.** At 4kg lighter, the bar will feel heavier than the numbers suggest.

---

## Part 2: Weekly Structure

| Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lift A | Easy run | Lift B | Rest / walk (optional run in Wks 2–3) | Lift C | Easy run | Rest |

- **Session A:** Squat focus plus bench
- **Session B:** Deadlift focus plus overhead press
- **Session C:** Light squat plus bench volume (Week 3: RPE-8 singles)
- **Warm-up for every lift:** 10 min easy bike or rower, then the ramp-up sets listed.
- **Running replaces all zone 2 work** from the original plan. Don't stack walks or bike sessions on top of the runs.
- If a run and a lift fall on the same day, lift first and run later, ideally 6+ hours apart.

---

## Part 3: Week 1 – Re-grooving (≈65%, RPE 5–6), Accelerated Entry

**Adjustment:** He feels good, so Week 1 starts at the top of the ranges and includes a load test. He can move into Week 2 early if he earns it. **Pre-illness loads are not used.**

### Session A (Mon)
- **Back Squat:** 3×6 @ **90kg**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 50×5, 65×3, 75×2
  - **Load test:** after working sets, 1×3 @ **105kg**
- **Bench Press:** 3×6 @ **65kg**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 40×5, 50×3
  - **Load test:** after working sets, 1×3 @ **75kg**
- Chest-Supported Row: 3×10, moderate
- Split Squat: 2×8/leg, bodyweight or light dumbbells
- Plank: 2×30s

**Load test pass:** Bar speed is fast and consistent, and the set feels RPE 6 or below.
**Load test fail:** The set feels RPE 7 or above or slows down. In that case, drop working loads to 85kg squat and 60kg bench for the rest of the week.

### Session B (Wed)
- **Deadlift:** 3×5 @ **110kg**
  - Ramp: 60×5, 80×3, 90×2, 100×1
- **Overhead Press:** 3×6 @ about 60% of his usual working weight (e.g. 35–37.5kg if he normally presses 60kg×5)
- Lat Pulldown: 3×10
- Back Extension: 2×10
- Face Pull: 2×15

### Session C (Fri)
- **Back Squat:** 2×5 @ **80kg** (technique focus)
- **Bench Press:** 3×8 @ **57.5–60kg**
- Dumbbell Row: 3×10/side
- Romanian Deadlift: 2×8, light
- Dead Bug: 2×8/side

### Early-Advance Rule

If **all** of the following are true, switch to Week 2 loads from Session B or C:
- Session A load test passed
- Resting HR is normal 48h after Session A
- No post-exertional crash
- Readiness is green

This can bring Week 3 loading forward to around day 14. Don't skip or shorten Week 2 or Week 3 themselves, and **don't accelerate the running**.

### Week 1 Running: Run-Walk (≈4–5km total)
- **Tue:** 10 min brisk walk, then 6 × (3 min easy run / 1 min walk), then 5 min walk (≈2.5km running)
- **Sat:** Repeat Tuesday's session. If Tuesday felt easy and recovery was normal, progress to 5 × (4 min run / 1 min walk).
- **Check:** He should feel normal the next morning and for the next lift. If not, repeat these runs in Week 2.

---

## Part 4: Week 2 – Rebuilding Capacity (≈70–77%, RPE 6–7)

Leave 3+ reps in reserve on every set.

### Session A
- **Back Squat:** 4×5 @ **100–107.5kg**
- **Bench Press:** 4×5 @ **72.5–75kg**
- Chest-Supported Row: 3×8–10
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 3×8/leg
- Hanging Knee Raise: 3×10

### Session B
- **Deadlift:** 3×4 @ **120–130kg**
- **Overhead Press:** 3×5 @ about 75% of his usual working weight
- Weighted or Assisted Pull-up: 3×6–8
- Back Extension: 3×10, loaded
- Face Pull: 3×15

### Session C
- **Back Squat:** 3×5 @ **95kg**
- **Close-Grip or Paused Bench:** 3×6 @ **65–70kg**
- Dumbbell Row: 3×10/side
- Romanian Deadlift: 3×8, moderate
- Pallof Press: 3×10/side

### Week 2 Running: Continuous Easy (≈6–7km total)
- **Tue:** 20–25 min continuous easy run (≈3–3.5km)
- **Thu (optional, green readiness only):** 15 min easy (≈2km). Skip it if Wednesday's deadlifts left him flat.
- **Sat:** 25–30 min continuous easy run (≈4km)

---

## Part 5: Week 3 – Return to Working Weights plus e1RM Reset (≈80–87%, RPE 7–8)

**Adjustment:** No true 1RM in this block. Instead, he works up to RPE-8 singles on all three lifts to generate estimated maxes (e1RM). The deadlift single replaces the original 3×3 in Session B.

### Session A
- **Back Squat:** 4×3 @ **115–122.5kg**
- **Bench Press:** 4×3 @ **82.5–87.5kg**
- Barbell Row: 3×6–8
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 3×6/leg, heavier than Week 2
- Ab Wheel: 3×8

### Session B: Deadlift e1RM
- **Deadlift:**
  - Ramp: 60×5, 100×3, 120×2, 135×1
  - Work up in 5–10kg jumps to a **top single @ RPE 8** (expect about 150–155kg)
  - Then 2×3 @ **140kg**
- **Overhead Press:** 4×4 @ about 85% of his usual working weight
- Weighted Pull-up: 3×5–6
- Back Extension: 3×8, loaded
- Face Pull: 3×15

### Session C: Squat and Bench e1RM (green readiness only)
- **Back Squat:**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 60×5, 85×3, 105×2, 117.5×1
  - Work up to a **top single @ RPE 8** (expect about 125–130kg)
  - Then 2×3 @ **110kg**
- **Bench Press:**
  - Ramp: bar×10, 50×5, 65×3, 77.5×2
  - Work up to a **top single @ RPE 8** (expect about 90kg)
  - Then 2×5 @ **77.5kg**
- Light RDL: 2×8
- Core: 2 sets of choice

**Rules for the singles:**
- Use safeties and a spotter.
- RPE 8 means he could have done about 2 more reps. Stop there and don't chase numbers.
- If readiness is amber or red, postpone the singles to the next green day or run Week 3 again.

### Calculating His Numbers

**e1RM ≈ RPE-8 single ÷ 0.92. Training max (TM) = 90% of e1RM.**

| Lift | Example RPE-8 single | e1RM | Training max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Squat | 127.5kg | ~138kg | ~125kg |
| Bench | 90kg | ~98kg | ~87.5kg |
| Deadlift | 155kg | ~168kg | ~150kg |

Replace these examples with his actual singles.

### Week 3 Running: Rebuilding Volume (≈8–10km total)
- **Tue:** 25–30 min easy (≈4km)
- **Thu (optional):** 15–20 min easy, plus 4 × 15s relaxed strides if he feels good
- **Sat:** 35–40 min easy (≈5–6km), the longest run of the block
  - This follows Friday's singles, so keep it strictly easy.
  - Cut it to 30 min if his legs are heavy.

---

## Part 6: Running Rules (All Weeks)

- **Every run is easy.** He should be able to talk in full sentences, ideally in zone 2 (65–75% of max HR or below his old easy-run HR).
- **Slower pace is expected.** Run to heart rate, not to his old paces.
- **Cardiac drift.** If HR climbs more than 10–15 bpm over 20 min at a steady easy pace on flat ground, stop and walk home.
- **No intervals, tempo runs or hills** during the block.

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Amber readiness | Swap the run for a 20–30 min walk |
| Red readiness | Walk only |
| Legs heavy before a lift | Cut the run's duration by a third |
| Worse 24–48h after a run | Repeat the previous week's running volume |

**Priority:** If something has to give, keep the lifting and trim the running. Running volume is the easiest thing to cut without losing progress.

---

## Part 7: Nutrition

**Assumptions:** 85kg pre-illness, 81kg now, 180cm. Recalculate with his real figures.
**Maintenance estimate:** Mifflin-St Jeor BMR of about 1,735 kcal × 1.55 activity factor ≈ **2,700 kcal**.

### Daily Targets

| Week | Calories | Protein | Fat | Carbs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~3,000 | 160–170g | 75–85g | ~390g |
| 2 | ~3,100 | 160–170g | 75–85g | 420–440g |
| 3 | ~3,200 | 160–170g | 75–85g | ~450–470g |

These totals already include the extra calories for running (about 60–70 kcal per km).

- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg, spread across 4–5 meals of 30–50g each.
- **Fat:** At least 0.8 g/kg (about 65g minimum).
- **Carbs:** Fill the remaining calories. This is the macro that fixes fatigue and refills glycogen, so don't cut it.
- **Carb shifting:**
  - Lift or run days: about 450–480g carbs, slightly less fat
  - Rest days: about 350–380g carbs, slightly more fat
  - Keep total calories roughly equal every day.

### Sample Day (~3,100 kcal, lift day)

| Meal | Example | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| Breakfast | 100g oats with milk, banana, honey, 3 eggs | ~40g |
| Mid-morning | 250g Greek yoghurt, granola, berries | ~25g |
| Lunch | 150g chicken, 250g cooked rice, veg, olive oil | ~50g |
| Pre-training (60–90 min before) | Bagel or 2 slices toast with jam | ~10g |
| Post-training | Whey shake in milk, plus fruit | ~35g |
| Dinner | 180g salmon or lean beef, potatoes, veg | ~40g |
| Evening (optional) | Cottage cheese or casein, peanut butter on toast | ~25g |

### If His Appetite Is Low
- Use smoothies made with milk, oats, banana, peanut butter and whey (700–900 kcal each).
- Lean on calorie-dense foods: nut butter, olive oil, cheese, dried fruit, whole milk.
- Eat 5–6 smaller meals instead of 3 large ones.
- Include white rice, pasta and bread so fibre doesn't fill him up before he hits his calories.

### Fluids and Supplements
- **Fluids:** About 2.8L/day baseline, plus 500–750ml per hour of running.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3–5g/day. Warn him it adds about 1kg on the scale early on.
- **Vitamin D:** Ideally based on bloods; reasonable in darker months.
- **Iron:** Only if his bloods show it's low.
- **Alcohol:** Keep it minimal.

### Monitoring

Weigh him 3× per week, first thing in the morning, and use the weekly average.

| Weekly change (after Week 1) | Action |
|---|---|
| Less than 0.2kg gain | Add 200 kcal/day, mostly carbs |
| 0.25–0.5kg gain | On track, hold steady |
| More than 0.7kg gain (excluding rebound and creatine) | Reduce by 150–200 kcal/day |
| Weight dropping | Check his actual intake first, then add 300 kcal/day |

- **Week 1:** A 1–2kg jump is expected. Don't cut calories in response.
- **Fatigue link:** If he feels poor and his weight has stalled, increase food before reducing training.
- **Expected outcome:** About 2.5–3.5kg regained by the end of the block. The rest usually returns over the following 2–4 weeks.

---

## Part 8: Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 hours. This is the biggest lever for post-viral fatigue.
- **Off days:** 10 min of mobility or an easy walk rather than complete rest, if his fatigue allows.
- **Life stress and alcohol:** Keep both low during the block.

---

## Part 9: Red Flags – Stop and Refer to GP

- Chest pain or tightness, palpitations, irregular beats on his watch, fainting or dizziness
- Breathlessness out of proportion to effort, including at easy running pace
- Resting HR elevated for several consecutive days
- Fatigue getting progressively worse across the block
- Repeated post-exertional crashes
- Fatigue boxes still failing after 4–6 weeks in total

---

## Part 10: End-of-Block Clearance

He is cleared for full-intensity lifting (RPE 9+, true maxes) when **all** of these are true:

- [ ] RPE-8 singles at 90% or more of pre-illness maxes (squat ≥125kg, bench ≥90kg, deadlift ≥152kg)
- [ ] Week 3 loads felt at or below target RPE, with consistent bar speed and normal technique
- [ ] No post-exertional crash in the last 7–10 days (any crash resets the clock)
- [ ] Resting HR at baseline for 7+ consecutive days; HRV stable if tracked
- [ ] Energy normal on 5+ days per week
- [ ] Weight stable or rising
- [ ] No cardiac or respiratory symptoms at any point

**For running intensity, also require:**
- [ ] Easy-run HR close to pre-illness levels
- [ ] HR drift of 8 bpm or less over a 40-min easy run
- [ ] 7–8km continuous run completed comfortably

If one or two boxes are unticked, repeat Week 3 and recheck.

## Part 11: After the Block (Weeks 4–8)

| Week | Lifting | Running |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Normal intermediate programme from the e1RM-based training maxes. RPE 8–9 top sets, no maxes. | 4km, 3km, 7–8km, all easy, plus 4–6 strides |
| 5 | Full training maxes | Continuous easy 10k (if the 8km went well). One quality session: short tempo **or** light intervals, not both. |
| 6+ | Max work allowed if all clearance boxes are ticked | Full conditioning returns |
| 6–8 | **True 1RM retest** to correct the training maxes upward | — |

- Keep the "worse 24–48 hours later" rule running through Weeks 4–6.
- If early sessions feel easy, add 2.5kg to squat and deadlift training maxes and 1–2.5kg to bench after 2–3 weeks.

## Appendix: Gated True 1RM in Week 3 (Optional, Not Recommended)

Use this only if you decide to override the e1RM approach. **Every gate must be met on test day:**
- Cardiac screen completed and clear
- Session A triples at RPE 8 or below
- No crashes in Weeks 2–3
- Resting HR at baseline that morning
- Readiness 4–5 with good sleep the night before
- Weight stable or rising

If any gate fails, revert to the e1RM method.

**Restructured Week 3**

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Session A, reduced to 3×3 (squat 115kg, bench 82.5kg) |
| Tue | Easy run, 25–30 min |
| Wed | Rest or 20 min walk |
| Thu | Deadlift 1RM test, then OHP 3×5 @ about 70% and face pulls |
| Fri | Rest |
| Sat | Squat 1RM test, then bench 1RM test (15 min break between) |
| Sun | Rest or easy walk |

Drop the Thursday run and move the long run into Week 4.

**Test rules:**
- 3–5 min rest between singles
- Maximum of 3 attempts after warm-up
- No missed reps; stop at RPE 9.5 or at any technique breakdown
- Safeties and a spotter required

| Lift | Warm-up | Opener | Second | Third (only if 2nd ≤ RPE 9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deadlift | 60×5, 100×3, 120×2, 135×1, 145×1 | 152.5–155kg | 160–165kg | 167.5–170kg |
| Squat | bar×10, 60×5, 85×3, 105×2, 117.5×1 | 125–127.5kg | 132.5–135kg | 137.5–140kg |
| Bench | bar×10, 50×5, 65×3, 77.5×2, 85×1 | 90kg | 95kg | 97.5–100kg |

**After the test:**
- Monitor resting HR, energy and sleep for 72 hours.
- If he crashes, run Week 4 as a repeat of Week 2 loading and discount the tested numbers by 5%.
- Set training maxes at 90% of the tested 1RMs.
- Expect these numbers to be 5–10% low, and correct them upward by Week 8.
